assumptions: Frame: Earth-centred inertial fixed at liftoff, z along the spin axis, x through the launch meridian at liftoff; no epoch, so the orbit's node in J2000 is not fixed here (module 37). Time: seconds from liftoff (holddown release).

Earth: a sphere of radius 6378136.6 m (Aster pck00010 a), point-mass gravity GM 398600441800000 m^3/s^2 (Aster delta-v.ts), rotating at 0.00007292115373194001 rad/s (pck00010); no J2, no oblate surface.
Atmosphere: the 1976 US Standard (idea 02's isa(), PartForge), no wind; above 85999.95 m (the top of its table) density and pressure taken as zero.

Drag: q S C_A(M), S from a 4 m diameter, C_A the Apollo/Saturn V wind-tunnel forebody coefficient digitized from Walker, NASA TM X-53770, Figure 28, held flat outside Mach 0.5 to 7.8; applied to this vehicle as a shape it may not have; no lift, no normal force at angle of attack.

Thrust: n [F_vac(tau) - p_a A_e] from idea 33 via idea 34; at throttle tau the engine flow scales with idea 33's chamber flow (gas-generator flow proportional, assumed); no thrust build-up or tail-off impulse; no engine cant.

Steering in a launch plane fixed in inertial space at liftoff (no yaw steering): vertical, a pitch kick held until the Earth-relative velocity turns as far, then zero angle of attack (gravity turn); upper stages pitch from 9.15 to 0 deg above the horizon, linear in time. Open loop: no guidance (module 36).

loss_gravity.source: 36-closed-loop/closedloop.js flyClosed() (UPFG) (against the Earth-relative speed, as idea 35)

open_loop_programme.source: 35-max-q/ascent.js fly() on the same plan (idea 35's open-loop upper programme)

refusals.reason: No engine dry mass is computed or given here: the fetched sources (SP-8107, SP-8110, SP-8120, TM-107318) give turbopump weights, not engine weights. (Here each stage's dry mass includes its engines: sourced for AS-512, otherwise typed or scaled.)
refusals.what_would_help: A sourced engine dry mass for module 34 (Stack), from the engine's data sheet or the vehicle's mass breakdown.

refusals.reason: At 49.99 bar chamber and 101.3 kPa ambient the nozzle separates (exit 16.83 kPa, SP-8120 separation at 27.62 kPa): a full-flowing thrust would be wrong and no separated-flow model is offered.
refusals.what_would_help: A higher throttle, a smaller area ratio, or an ambient below 66.93 kPa.

refusals.reason: This vehicle's drag coefficient is the Saturn V's (the only wind-tunnel curve here), scaled by its diameter.
refusals.what_would_help: A wind-tunnel or CFD axial-force curve for this vehicle's shape.

refusals.reason: Guidance cut Stage 2 off with 4929.9 kg unburned, but idea 34's vehicle gives that stage no second burn: whether it can restart for a departure is not stated.
refusals.what_would_help: A second burn for this stage in idea 34 (a restartable engine, with its coast losses), or a separate departure stage.

refusals.reason: Navigation is perfect here: guidance knows the true state. The flight's own cutoff was 30.8 m and 0.20 m/s from its prediction (section 9.3).
refusals.what_would_help: An inertial-platform error model (ST-124M drift and accelerometer errors) to fly guidance on a navigated state.

refusals.reason: The dispersion sizes are one flight's deviations from its prediction (AS-512), used as one sigma: a population of flights is not in the report.
refusals.what_would_help: MSFC's three-sigma dispersion tables for Saturn V (the operational trajectory documents), or the deviations of several flights.

assumptions: Frame and time as idea 35: Earth-centred inertial fixed at liftoff (z the spin axis, x through the launch meridian at liftoff), seconds from liftoff; no epoch, so the node in J2000 is module 37's. The orbit's node here is measured from that x axis.

First stage: idea 35's open-loop flight, unchanged (plan in the ascent handoff). Upper stages: Unified Powered Flight Guidance (NTRS 19740004402) from 0 s after first-stage cutoff (attitude held until then), a command every 2 s held fixed in inertial space, the last cycles frozen; cutoff when the orbital energy reaches the target's.
Navigation is perfect: guidance knows the true position and velocity, and senses the true thrust acceleration; its model of the vehicle is idea 34's nominal ledger.
Earth, gravity and atmosphere as idea 35 (sphere, point mass, 1976 atmosphere below 86 km, no wind, no J2).
